title: Token-rate imbalance causing TTFT regressions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private - emergency mitigation & postmortem
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden first-token and sustained token/sec degradation beginning 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC that affected Hosted API, several Dedicated pools, and two Private deployments. Symptoms included long TTFT for short prompts (30–600ms -> 600–1200ms), and sustained tokens/sec drop (~30%).
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy model variants (gpt-meduim-8b/quant-int8 and gpt-latency-compat-13b) with a heterogeneous fanout enabled under the new kernel-selector change (runtime-2.3.0). 2) Send parallel 200 RPS of 16-token prompts, mixed seq lengths (16/256/1024) and varying temperature. 3) Observe KV prefetch latencies and scheduler backpressure on model shards. 4) Notice prioritized short-session requests are queued behind warmup-prefetch for long contexts.
impact_summary: - Multiple enterprise customers reported application timeouts and elevated errors. - SLO breach on hosted default route for first-byte 99th percentile in EU region. - Dedicated customer X experienced a 28% throughput loss for short interactive sessions. - Private customer Y observed sporadic tail-latency spikes coinciding with quantized-variant rollouts.
mitigation:
Short-term (hotpatch):
- Reverted the recent kernel-selector heuristic for mixed-precision models (rolled back in runtime-2.3.1-hotfix). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12345
- Enabled a temporary adaptive-token-shedder for short-session traffic to prioritize first-token processing (feature-flag: token_shedder_v2=true).
- Increased KV prefetch timeout to reduce backpressure for heterogenous fanout shards.
Long-term:
- Introduce probe-based kernel-selection that benchmarks candidate kernels on first N requests before committing.
- Add per-deployment warmup budget accounting to avoid cross-tenant prefetch storms.
- Expand e2e load tests for mixed sequence-length fanouts and quantized models.
